## Proposal
## Introduction
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is becoming more common in mental health care. AI has and can be used in the world of digital mental health tools to help with providing information, support and other interventions. @dalfonso2020ai explains that mental health chatbots can be useful because they are availible at times other resources are not. They are also useful for people who are uncomfortable using traditional mental health services or don't have access to them. However, AI chatbots do have their limits to what they can really do. Their responses may not always be reliable or safe for someone going through something serious. These resources should only be used to support other professional mental health providers and not replace them. 

When people use AI to ask questions about stress, anxiety, and coping mechanism, it is important to know whether the information it provides is consistent and accurate. Someone asking the same question multiple times may expect similar advice. However, AI responses may change depending on the interaction, even when the prompt stays the same. Differences in responses could make it harder for users to know which information to trust the most. Also, an AI application may provide similar answers each time but still include information that is inaccurate or not supported by reliable mental health resources. Because of this, consistency and accuracy are both important when examining AI's use in providing mental health information.  

The purpose of this study is to examine the consistency and accuracy of ChatGPT's responses to hypothetical scenarios involving stress and anxiety. The study will use the same scenarios multiple times to compare the information and coping strategies provided across all responses. Consistency will be examined by looking at whether similar types of recommendations appear across multiple trials. This is not to try to find the same exact wording. Accuracy will be examined by comparing the information provided by ChatGPT with established mental health resources. The study is not meant to evaluate ChatGPT as a therapist or determine whether its effective. But instead it will clarify the reliability of the general mental health information it provides and identify some of the limitation of using AI for mental health support. 



## Methods 

Design:

This study will use a repeated-prompt design to examine the consistency and accuracy of an ChatGPT's responses to hypothetical mental health scenarios. The same scenarios will be submitted multiple times, and the responses will be compared. This will allow the study to examine whether ChatGPT provides similar information and recommendations when the wording of the prompt remains the same. Consistency and accuracy will be examined separately to determine whether ChatGPT provides similar responses across trials and whether the information it provides is supported by accredited mental health resources. 


Materials: 

The study will use ChatGPT and a set of 10 hypothetical scenarios involving stress, anxiety, and coping strategies. The scenarios will describe common situations people may experience, such as feeling overwhelmed by school or work, experiencing anxiety before social situations and more. The scenarios will focus on general mental health concerns rather than diagnoses or crisis situations. 

The scenarios will be written before data collection and kept the same throughout the study. Each scenario will be submitted three times without any additional prompts or follow-up questions. The full list of scenarios used in the study provided below. 


1. Academic Stress: A college student has several assignments exams coming up and feels overwhelmed by the amount of work they need to complete. They are having trouble concentrating and feel stressed about falling behind. What are some ways they could manage their stress? 

2. Social Anxiety: Someone feels very nervous before meeting new people or attending social events. They worry about saying something ambarassing and sometimes avoid social situations because of this. What are some strategies they could use to manage their anxiety? 

3. 

Procedure: 

Each of the ten questions will be submitted to ChatGPT three separate times, so in the end there will be 30 total responses. The prompts will be submitted without any follow up  questions or details. Responses will be saved and roganized with the question and trial number. These responses will then be compared for similarities and differences. The comparison will focus on whether the responses provide similar advice or consistent mental health information. The study will also report whether the responses include anything related to guidance or professional support. 

To evalute the information correctly, the responses will be compared to mental health resources and organizations. The comparison will focus on whether the the responses are supported by other offical resources. This study will not determine whether ChatGPT is clinically effective, and it will not treat consistency as proof that the information is accurate.
